💬 Ghalibaf: US fully exposed despite projecting hegemony

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Ghalibaf says the United States appears to project hegemony and superior power but is in reality “fully exposed.”

Ghalibaf made the remarks in a post on X, reacting to a recent JPMorgan assessment that said the bank had, for the first time since the start of the US-Israeli war of aggression on Iran, no baseline view for forecasting the oil market.
​
“We simply don’t know how to model the endgame,” JPMorgan analysts said in a September 17 note, according to Reuters.
​
Ghalibaf described the situation as resembling the Schrödinger’s cat paradox, saying, “It’s Schrödinger: the empire is in the SOH (Strait of Hormuz) cabinet with falling plates, projecting hegemony but fully exposed, trying to suffocate Iran without blowback (impossible).”
​
“This endgame cannot be modeled. It will be opened, and Iran’s hand is already on the lever,” he added.
​
The United States and Israel waged an unprovoked war on Iran on February 28, assassinating top Iranian officials and commanders, including the Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei.
​
After forty days, Iran’s decisive response, including its unrelenting military operations and closure of the Strait of Hormuz, forced Washington and Tel Aviv to halt the war.

🔊 FM Araghchi expresses condolences over passing of Grand Ayatollah Shobeiri Zanjani

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has expressed condolences over the passing of Grand Ayatollah Seyyed Mousa Shobeiri Zanjani, describing the senior Shia religious scholar as a guardian of the valuable heritage of Shia jurisprudence.

In a condolence message issued on Monday, Araghchi said the prominent jurist had left a lasting legacy of profound knowledge, piety, humility and sincerity after a lifetime devoted to scholarship, teaching students and preserving Shia jurisprudential heritage.
​
He described the passing as a major loss for Islamic seminaries, the academic and religious community, and followers of the infallible household of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).
​
Araghchi extended his condolences to the Leader of the Islamic Revolution, senior religious authorities, Islamic seminaries, scholars and students, the Iranian people, and followers of the late source of emulation around the world.
​
He also prayed for the deceased scholar’s high spiritual rank and reunion with God’s righteous servants, while asking God to grant patience and reward to his family and bereaved relatives.
​
The office of Grand Ayatollah Shobeiri Zanjani announced early Monday that the prominent jurist and senior religious authority had passed away.

Mikhail Avilov – The Duel of Peresvet and Chelubey at the Battle of Kulikovo  

Price: $5,000,000  

Painted in 1943 during the Great Patriotic War, this work turns the historic 1380 duel into a symbol of clashing worlds, wills, and fates. The moment of impact is frozen: lances collide, horses rear, fabric and grass torn by motion. It’s not just battle—it’s the instant before destiny strikes.  

Peresvet sits calm, centered. Chelubey is tense, impulsive. The contrast is stark.  

The piece earned the Stalin Prize and became a defining image of the Battle of Kulikovo in Soviet art. Avilov studied ancient Russian armor and costumes for accuracy. At a time of national struggle, historical triumphs like this one carried deep meaning.  

Today, it’s housed in the State Russian Museum.  

More than a duel—it’s a visual declaration of resilience. The energy is so intense, you feel the clash through the canvas.

🎙 Iran president: Learning, skills can help solve problems

📌 Tehran, IRNA – President Masoud Pezeshkian has told students that acquiring knowledge and practical skills can help address problems facing people, families, cities, the country and the world.

Speaking at a ceremony marking the start of the new school year at Hazrat Fatemeh Zahra School in Tehran’s District 11 on Monday, the president said he had risen to the presidency from an ordinary employee family.
​
He urged students to strive for excellence, saying they should build a future in which no foreigner would dare view Iranians as weak. He also stressed friendship, cooperation and support, warning that conflict among students could undermine their efforts.
​
Pezeshkian emphasized proper education, saying the government would seek to provide an environment based on friendship, participation and effort.
​
He encouraged students to help their families, friends and teachers and use what they learn to solve problems around them.
​
Learning without skills is not effective, he said, urging them to develop abilities and apply their knowledge to help others.
​
The president said solving people’s problems and contributing to national development were goals, and called on students to work together, study well and develop problem-solving skills.
